exam: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
q: As per the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was decided to be the joint capital of the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for ____ years following which it shall belong to Telangana.
explanation: Sec 5: Hyderabad is the common capital for a period not exceeding ten years, after which it is Telangana's capital; of the options, 10.

exam: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
q: As per the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, ____ became the capital of the newly formed state of Telangana, after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh. The city will remain as the joint capital of both states for a period of time not exceeding ten years.
explanation: Sec 5(2): after the common-capital period Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana, and AP gets a new capital.

q: How many districts does the state of Andhra Pradesh have after its Bifurcation in 2014?
explanation:
13 districts in 2014 — now 28 districts (26 from 4 Apr 2022; Polavaram and Markapuram added 31 Dec 2025) (job b1-r263 notes, citing theprint.in Dec 2025)
After bifurcation AP had 13 districts (Telangana 10).

exam: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
q: At present, Hyderabad is which type of capital of Andhra Pradesh?
explanation:
Hyderabad was AP's de jure capital only till 2 June 2024 — now it is Telangana's capital alone and Amaravati is AP's capital (AP Reorganisation Act s.5(2); old app notes 3:134 on the 2026 amendment)
Under Sec 5 Hyderabad was AP's capital in law (de jure) during the common-capital period, while AP actually governed from Amaravati (de facto).
